done_when: A follow-up that names a period answers for that period whatever window the model emits; a question naming no period still inherits or aggregates as before; changing an answer's period still re-runs on the chosen period

findings.body: Detected-but-unparsed period language still preserves the model's window at this branch. `hasTimePeriodWords` recognizes expressions such as “previous week”, “next month”, “YTD”, and “FY”, but neither parser resolves them, so a wrong model window remains authoritative. There are also deterministic misparses: “third quarter of 2025” returns before considering the explicit year and anchors to the prior/current year, while any four-digit financial value such as “amounts over 2025” is treated as a calendar year, breaking the no-period inheritance/aggregation case. The new detector-only test explicitly lists several unresolved expressions without verifying their selected windows, so the full Done-when behavior remains unmet.

findings.body: The added regression scenarios beginning here call `ChatService.ask` through `makeFixture`, whose model, executor, warehouse, and audit boundaries are fakes. Repository inspection still finds no Playwright test/configuration or browser test command covering a named-period follow-up, no-period inheritance/aggregation, and changing an answer's period. The frontend tests mock the Ask API. Consequently, this user-facing behavior remains proven only by unit/component tests rather than through a browser, running API, real database, prior-turn transport, and period control as required.
findings.title: Not done: end-to-end Ask coverage for period selection and reruns

why: An Ask question that names a period, such as July 2026, answers for that period even as a follow-up in the same thread; the model's own window and the previous answer's window used to win
